transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. To start, could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

I guess… I’m here because I’m having a hard time keeping things organized. There are a lot of moving parts—patent notes, workshop prep, gallery deadlines, decisions with the team—and I keep ending up working on whatever feels most urgent or loudest, not necessarily what actually matters. It’s gotten hard to manage.
When did you first start noticing these difficulties with organization and prioritizing tasks—has this been a lifelong pattern, or did it start more recently?

I think it goes back pretty far. Looking back at old school comments, teachers would say I was bright, but I’d daydream or forget to hand in work I’d already done. I lost homework folders a lot too. So… yeah, before I was a teenager, definitely.

Do you notice these same problems with focus and organization in other parts of your life outside of work—like at home or in personal relationships—or is it mostly tied to your current work situation?

It’s not only work, but work is where it shows up the most. What pushed me to come in is just… I can’t keep all the moving parts organized anymore—notes, deadlines, prep, decisions with people—and I end up jumping to whatever feels most pressing instead of what actually matters.
Do you often feel physically restless, fidgety, or find yourself acting or speaking impulsively without thinking things through?

Some, yeah. Mostly on long design calls. I’ll start feeling this sort of pressure to get up, and I’ll end up pacing around my office or switching chairs, even if I’m trying to look like I’m paying attention.

In the past six months, have you noticed yourself frequently losing things you need, like keys, documents, or your phone, or forgetting appointments and commitments in your day-to-day life outside of work?

Yeah… that happens a lot. I’m always looking for things I need, like USB-C adapters, my stylus, sketchbook, sometimes my badge. I’ll set something down and then have no idea where it went, and it can throw off a whole morning.

Have these attention and organization difficulties caused noticeable problems in your relationships or home life—like forgetting commitments to family or friends, or conflicts because of disorganization?

More at work than home, honestly. It’s… it’s started affecting how people see me there. I missed a patent filing checkpoint, and then there was a rough architecture review where I wasn’t on top of things. After that, some collaborators seemed to be questioning whether I should be leading the bigger project.

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient reports a lifelong pattern (since before adolescence) of inattention, disorganization, distractibility, forgetfulness, and losing items, corroborated by childhood history (teacher comments about daydreaming, incomplete homework submission despite completion, lost folders). Symptoms are present across multiple settings (work and home), though most impairing at work, satisfying the cross-situational criterion. Mild hyperactive-impulsive symptoms (restlessness, need to pace during calls) are present but not predominant, consistent with a combined presentation. Functional impairment is clearly documented (missed patent filing checkpoint, poor performance in review, colleagues questioning leadership capability). This pattern is most consistent with ADHD, combined presentation (F90.0), distinguishing it from predominantly inattentive (F90.1) given some hyperactive-impulsive symptoms, and from hyperkinetic conduct disorder (F90.2) given absence of conduct disturbance.
